title: Local and Remote Build Cache Correctness Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies local and remote build cache correctness?
options: Share only deterministic declared outputs through an authenticated cache with trusted writers and measured value.
Use hit rate as the sole metric
questions.answer: Share only deterministic declared outputs through an authenticated cache with trusted writers and measured value.
questions.explanation: The correct approach preserves Gradle’s lazy model, explicit data flow, variant correctness, functional evidence and operability.

questions.prompt: The Gradle dependency cache and build cache store the same kind of reusable data.
questions.explanation: Allowing forked pull requests to push into the same remote cache lets untrusted code publish outputs later consumed by trusted release jobs.

questions.prompt: Why should trusted CI often be the only remote-cache writer?
questions.answer: It reduces cache-poisoning risk while still letting developers and other jobs consume verified reusable outputs.
questions.explanation: The answer names the model property that makes the build behaviour predictable rather than relying on incidental script order.
